conclusions: 1375MHz passes complete reference underBW0 andBW5;1350MHz first tone missing underboth. Wide bandwidth did not restore reception underthese conditions.
Changing BW changes multiple analog/digital settings, not an isolated filter bypass. Fixed filters, frontend routing and LO failure remain possible.
1375MHz BW0 succeeds with VCO code1: low VCO code is not a standalone lock/failure criterion; withdraw that inference.

Retained B3 pair across modes0..5 produces93 same-order MMIO writes, only30360/302c4/302c8 differ; current PAC B body and port tables match SDK, native mode writes match. This is no frequency-dependent filter switch in that tested body, not exclusion of fixed analog filters or LO failure.

rx_fir.selection: NV+0x176.bit14 chooses EESF or normal coefficient image; not an established bypass

dlpf.meaning: Reset and band selection per reference; reset assertion is not transparent bypass; signal-path role unproven.

controls.pll_filter_ibit_rx: PLL control name, not proof of an IQ passband filter
controls.external_frontend: No confirmed Air724UG external digital HPF/LPF/BPF bypass found; RFFE switches can select fixed paths without bypassing physical filters.

rx_pre_fir.scope: DWARF and offline native instructions plus current source; not a new live readback or proof of every digital filter being bypassed
rx_pre_fir.conclusion: FIR table loading alone does not establish activation. Do not repeat clearing a bit already clear in the direct prepare profile. Native DAGC only changes bits4:0 and preserves FIR_EN.

next: No defined independent filter bypass found. Trace LO/analog consumers; do not flash unnamed reset toggles or repeat identical boundary/BW experiments. Integrate verified lower B3 points into shared host capabilities and Auto while retaining discrete-evidence labels.
